scenes.title: A little calmer. A lot more yours.
scenes.body: A calm Fedora desktop, with useful defaults and room to make it yours.
scenes.narration: Meet Arctic Linux. A calm, keyboard-first desktop built on Fedora, with the Mango tiling window manager. Let's take a look at installation, the lighter everyday apps, and a few details that make the desktop your own.

scenes.title: Try it first.
scenes.body: One live USB. Two clear choices.
scenes.shortcut: Try Arctic Linux · Install Arctic Linux
scenes.narration: Start with a live USB. The boot menu lets you try Arctic Linux or open the installer. You can explore the desktop before deciding to put it on your computer.

scenes.title: Take a look around.
scenes.body: The live session gives you a working desktop and an easy way to install.
scenes.narration: The live welcome card gives you a few useful shortcuts. Keep trying the desktop, or choose Install Arctic Linux. The install button is also right there on the top bar.

scenes.title: One question at a time.
scenes.body: Choose your language. Go back whenever you need.
scenes.narration: The installer starts with your language. Each screen asks one clear question, and the sidebar shows where you are. These installer screens use sample disks, networks, and account details.

scenes.title: Make the keys feel right.
scenes.body: Pick your layout and test it before entering passwords.
scenes.narration: Choose your keyboard layout, then try it in the test box. The live session uses your choice too. If you switch to a text console or disconnect a screen, the installer keeps your page and your answers.

scenes.title: Connect now. Or finish setup later.
scenes.body: Online installation downloads extras. Offline installation keeps a clear setup queue.
scenes.narration: Connect to Wi-Fi, or plug in a cable. You can also choose Install offline. The apps already on the image remain available, while extra downloads wait until you're connected. Your new system remembers the Wi-Fi connection.

scenes.title: Set your local time.
scenes.body: Check the suggested region and city. Keep the clock in sync.
scenes.narration: Next, check your time zone. The installer suggests a location, and you can change the region or city. Automatic time keeps the clock in sync.

scenes.title: Choose where Arctic lives.
scenes.body: Erase a disk, or use free space alongside another system when available.
scenes.tag: Back up your files before installing
scenes.narration: Choose your disk and how to install. Erasing replaces its contents. Installing alongside another system is offered when suitable free space is available. Back up your files before you continue.

scenes.title: Private, from the start.
scenes.body: Disk encryption is on by default. Keep your passphrase somewhere safe.
scenes.narration: Disk encryption is on by default. Create a passphrase, or use the suggested one. You'll enter it when the computer starts. Keep it safe: forgotten passphrases cannot be recovered.

scenes.title: Make it your computer.
scenes.body: Your name, sign-in password, and computer name.
scenes.narration: Create your account, set your sign-in password, and name the computer. Automatic login is optional. You can also choose to use your account password for the encrypted disk.

scenes.title: Choose the apps you want.
scenes.body: GNOME Web, Foot, PCManFM, FeatherPad and Celluloid. Alternatives stay available.
scenes.narration: The suggested apps now keep the everyday setup lighter: GNOME Web for browsing, Foot for the terminal, PCManFM for files, FeatherPad for text, and Celluloid for media. Choose alternatives if you prefer. Office suites and code editors are optional.

scenes.title: Review. Then install.
scenes.body: Nothing is written to your disk until you confirm on the Summary screen.
scenes.narration: The summary brings your choices together. Check the disk, encryption, account, and apps, and change anything you need. Nothing is written to the disk until you confirm the install here.

scenes.title: Let Arctic do the setup.
scenes.body: Follow the progress as the system and selected apps are installed.
scenes.narration: The progress screen shows the system and your selected apps being installed. An optional app download can be retried or skipped. VoxType setup runs separately, so a missing model never stops the operating system from installing.

scenes.title: Your desktop is ready.
scenes.body: Read the final notes, including any queued downloads or driver approval.
scenes.narration: When installation finishes, read the final notes. They tell you about queued downloads and any Secure Boot steps for a driver. Remove the USB and restart when you're ready. These screens are a demonstration, rather than a recording of a fresh install.

scenes.title: Room for your day.
scenes.body: A quiet bar. Five workspaces. Photo wallpapers from the project collection.
scenes.narration: On the desktop, five workspaces give each task some room. The bar stays small, and the backgrounds now come from the project's photo collection. Existing users keep their own wallpaper choices when they update.

scenes.title: Open it. Find it. Keep moving.
scenes.body: Search apps, files, open windows, and settings from one launcher.
scenes.narration: Press Super and Space to open the launcher. Type an app name and press Enter. It also finds files, open windows, and settings, so you can get to the next task quickly.

scenes.title: Small tasks, handled here.
scenes.body: Calculate, convert units, run commands, and set reminders.
scenes.narration: The launcher handles small jobs too. Start with an equals sign to calculate, and press Enter to copy the answer. You can convert units, run commands, or set a reminder for later.

scenes.title: Windows make room for each other.
scenes.body: Mango tiles new windows automatically. The amber border shows your focus.
scenes.narration: Open a few windows and Mango arranges them automatically. The amber border marks the one you're using. Move between windows with Super and the arrow keys, or switch workspaces to separate your tasks.
scenes.tag: Separate real app captures · composed layout

scenes.title: Your files, in PCManFM.
scenes.body: Tabs, folders, removable drives and XArchiver for archives.
scenes.narration: PCManFM is the new graphical file manager, using Fedora's GTK three build. Browse folders and downloads in tabs, and use XArchiver to open or create archives. Super and F opens whichever file manager you've chosen.

scenes.title: A terminal with a familiar face.
scenes.body: Foot, Fish and the Arctic fox greeting. Bash, Flatpak and Nix are available too.
scenes.narration: Super and Enter opens Foot with Fish and the Arctic fox greeting. Bash and Nano are there too. Fedora packages, Flatpak and Nix give you several ways to add tools, without making a large app collection compulsory.

scenes.title: Browse. Write. Watch.
scenes.body: Useful native defaults. Choose more apps when you need them.
scenes.narration: GNOME Web shares the WebKit engine already used by Arctic's web apps. FeatherPad handles everyday text, and Celluloid plays music and video. Chromium remains available for web apps that need calling support. You can change the defaults in Settings.

scenes.title: Need one more app?
scenes.body: Get apps brings Flathub, Fedora packages, web apps, and terminal tools together.
scenes.narration: Need something else? Open Get apps and choose Flathub, Fedora packages, a web app, or a terminal tool. Installations continue when you close the launcher. Removing software has its own menu, so it's easier to find the action you want.

scenes.title: Remove apps has its own place.
scenes.body: See what will be removed before you confirm.
scenes.narration: Open Remove apps from the launcher to manage Fedora packages, Flatpaks, web apps, and terminal entries. Arctic shows the proposed removal before you confirm. It protects the desktop, your login shell, and your only terminal from an accidental removal.

scenes.title: Prepare dictation during installation.
scenes.body: Signed official VoxType. Verified local multilingual Whisper. Ready only after setup.
scenes.narration: Arctic installs pinned, signature-checked official VoxType 1.1.0 binaries and a verified multilingual Whisper model. During an online installation, Arctic automatically downloads and verifies the compatible CPU engine and model. An offline installation leaves a clear retry for first boot and reports that dictation is not ready. The local multilingual model supports Hebrew and English without sending audio to a service. Recording remains unavailable until the engine, model, and per-user VoxType configuration are ready.
evidence: Signature-checked official VoxType 1.1.0 binaries and verified local model
Automatic online setup finishes independently of OS installation
Offline setup stays visibly not ready until retry succeeds

scenes.title: Press. Speak. Press again.
scenes.body: Mango checks readiness, then runs VoxType's official toggle. Arctic status stays visible.
scenes.narration: Focus a text field and press Arctic's Mango shortcut, whose readiness guard runs VoxType's official record toggle. Press the same shortcut again to stop, transcribe, and insert with VoxType. Arctic's dictation pill follows VoxType's recording and transcription state, even when the taskbar is hidden. Audio and transcription stay on this computer. VoxType runs in quiet mode, and Arctic's notifications and status output do not include transcript text.
evidence: Readiness helper calls official voxtype record toggle
Arctic indicator follows official VoxType runtime state
Local insertion with quiet VoxType and transcript-free Arctic status

scenes.title: Clear status. A way to recover.
scenes.body: Explicit GPU or CPU setup, with measured limitations.
scenes.narration: VoxType uses one local multilingual Whisper model for Hebrew, English, and automatic language detection. Supported hardware can enable VoxType's Vulkan backend. If GPU setup fails, the error stays visible and the user can explicitly switch VoxType to CPU. In a hosted Westmere CPU test, the small model measured 7.77 percent English word error and 42.0 percent Hebrew word error. It took 15.79 times the English audio duration and 11.63 times the Hebrew duration, so that CPU result was not real time.
evidence: Local multilingual Whisper · Hebrew and English
Vulkan when supported · explicit CPU recovery
Hosted Westmere small-model test: 7.77% EN WER · 42.0% HE WER
CPU fixture was slower than real time

scenes.title: Find the setting. Change it.
scenes.body: Search across Settings. Changes apply straight away, with undo.
scenes.narration: Super and S opens Arctic Settings. Search for a setting instead of hunting through pages. Changes apply straight away, and Control and Z undoes the last one.

scenes.title: The bar can move out of the way.
scenes.body: Four edges. Always visible, auto-hide, or dodge windows.
scenes.narration: Put the bar on any edge, and choose always visible, auto-hide, or dodge windows. Move the pointer to its edge, or use the keyboard, to reveal it. Arctic's dictation indicator remains visible. The installer keeps its bar available while you're in the live session.

scenes.title: Winter or Polar night.
scenes.body: Winter, Polar night, and colours drawn from a photo of your own.
scenes.narration: Choose Winter or Polar night, or let a wallpaper provide the desktop's colours. The palette follows through the shell, window borders, terminal, and supported apps. Your own pictures stay selected when you change themes.

scenes.title: A fresh coat.
scenes.body: Photo backgrounds you can hide and restore per account.
scenes.narration: Winter keeps the same layout with soft, snow-coloured surfaces. The wallpaper picker includes the project's growing photo collection, alongside pictures you add yourself. You can set a favourite, or let the wallpaper change on a schedule. Built-in wallpapers can be deleted from your view and restored later, without affecting another account.
evidence: Delete hides a packaged wallpaper for this account

scenes.title: Ember Clouds, City Silhouette.
scenes.body: An original photograph from the Arctic wallpaper collection.
scenes.narration: One new choice is Ember Clouds, City Silhouette: warm clouds above the dark outline of the city. It's the artist's finished photograph, preserved at its original resolution. Set it from the wallpaper picker, or browse the full collection on the project's gallery.

scenes.title: The controls you reach for.
scenes.body: Volume, brightness, wireless connections, night light, and power mode.
scenes.narration: Quick settings puts the everyday controls together: volume, brightness, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and power mode. Night light makes evenings more comfortable, while Keep awake is handy during a presentation or long task.

scenes.title: Stay connected.
scenes.body: Join networks and manage connections from the bar.
scenes.narration: The network menu lets you join Wi-Fi and manage saved connections or a VPN. Nearby bar menus handle Bluetooth devices, speakers, microphones, and sound levels for individual apps.

scenes.title: Settle into your desk.
scenes.body: Arrange monitors, adjust scaling, and choose how the laptop screen behaves.
scenes.narration: At your desk, arrange monitors and adjust their resolution, scale, and rotation. Super and P switches screen modes. Arctic also handles USB drives, printing, and scanning, with settings when you need them.

scenes.title: Learn a few keys. Add your own.
scenes.body: Search the shortcut sheet, then tailor the desktop to your routine.
scenes.narration: You don't have to memorise every shortcut. Super and slash opens a searchable guide. Settings lets you add your own shortcuts, choose default apps, and decide what starts when you sign in.

scenes.title: Updates fit around your work.
scenes.body: Signed stable updates, with a one-time What's New summary.
scenes.narration: Arctic's signed stable repository keeps existing systems up to date. Updates download in the background and install when you restart. After each update, What's New shows the changes once, with release notes ready to reopen later. Settings shows the latest check and anything waiting. Save your work before choosing Restart and install. There is no need to reinstall for desktop package updates.
evidence: What's New appears once after each installed update
Release notes remain available from Settings → Updates
Signed stable packages install at restart

scenes.title: Step away with peace of mind.
scenes.body: The clock stays visible. Notifications keep their text private while locked.
scenes.narration: Super and L locks the desktop. The clock stays visible, and notifications show a count without their contents. Arctic also locks before sleeping. Your session stays protected when you step away.

scenes.title: Make room for your day.
scenes.body: Downloads, setup help, shortcuts and the full wiki on GitHub.
scenes.narration: That's Arctic Linux: a guided installer, a calm desktop, useful native apps, and local dictation when setup is complete. Find published downloads and the full wiki on GitHub. The release page tells you which image has been published, and which checks were performed.
